newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil begins to clear miners from Indian land.
newsitem.headline: Brazil begins to clear miners from Indian land.

text.p: Brazilian police on Friday launched a two-week operation to clear thousands of gold prospectors and loggers from a remote Indian reservation which has been devastated by their activity, officials said.

About 250 police officers travelled to the Sarare reservation, near Brazil's border with Bolivia in Mato Grosso state, where between 8,000 and 12,000 intruders were wiping out the culture of the tiny Kathitaullu tribe, said Villi Seilert, an adviser to the government's National Indian Foundation (Funai).

"The Indians' means of survival is being destroyed," said Seilert. He said leaders of the 78-member tribe had been tricked into selling truckloads of protected mahogany trees for currency no longer in circulation.
Long-standing tensions between the Indians and the trespassers turned violent in November when miners beat up a group of Kathitaullu men who had seized their digging equipment, Seilert said.
Mario Serprini, a federal police inspector in charge of the operation, said the trespassers would have until Jan. 15 to leave the reservation before facing arrest.

In 1992, police carried out a similar clearance of miners and loggers from the Sarare reservation, but failed to prevent them from quickly returning to the area where an estimated 800 open-face mines have been operating recently.
This time police will set up permanent checkpoints on four dirt roads leading to the reservation to prevent the miners and loggers from returning, Serprini said.
